forms.whenToUse: The statement hero: kicker/h1/standfirst/CTA row/data-strip/media, every placement owned by the form — the builder fills slots and pairs components, never writes hero layout CSS.
The editorial half + evidence half: heading and prose beside a figure and/or spec-table — the spec rows measure-capped at 44ch so they never sprawl.
The header band introducing an index/reel/archive: the meta-line is grid-placed off the heading's columns and hard-capped at 40ch — full-width sprawl has no reachable state.
The beats-SOTD statement band: giant display type carrying the image inside its letterforms (background-clip:text with a solid-ink @supports fallback). Set the media via --ad-type-image on the mark.
The funnel's close: one imperative (18ch cap), decisive channel rows, a quiet trust line a full rest below — no media slot exists, so the close cannot become a mood reel.

forms.winner: Anthropic, Lusion, Depo Luxe, Truekind, Eloy Benoffi
forms.whenToUse: The row-list body under index-reel-header: index/title/meta/thumb locked to one shared grid so column edges cannot drift and the meta cannot sprawl. Rows repeat the row slot; pairs index-row-hover.
Release/journal/blog cards in a 2-3 column grid: media 3/2, kicker/title/date at fixed rhythm; minmax(0,1fr) columns so a long title wraps instead of blowing the grid.

forms.winner: Terminal Industries, Anime.js, Lando Norris, FlowFest
forms.whenToUse: The restrained proof strip: a static wrapped wall of height-capped, quieted logos (grayscale at rest, colour on hover — the one micro-state the form owns). Never a marquee.
The standalone big-number strip: display-scale tabular values over mono captions, hairline-divided columns that never crowd (8ch floors). The dd carries data-ad-counter for the roll.
The 12-col asymmetric feature grid — cards carry REAL product-UI slices (never icons), spans 4-12 with dense backfill; the bento-fatigue correction.

forms.winner: Awwwards Mobile Excellence criterion (scored verbatim: swipe to see more, tap to enlarge); Codrops GSAP carousel canon
forms.whenToUse: The mobile-first image gallery: native scroll-snap track riding OS momentum (zero JS physics), next-cell peek, enhancer-fed snap dots. The scored Mobile Excellence line; pinned-filmstrip stays the desktop hold-and-drag signature.
One project per viewport: full-bleed media with a corner (or centered) caption over a structural contrast scrim — the gallery-stack unit; stack several for the procession.

The gallery-stack's opening slot: a type-forward name card — the name as the fold's whole argument, a role line, mono meta + scroll cue pinned to the bottom edge. Layout only; takes no position on what follows the fold.

The designed rest before the close: divided native details/summary rows (mono index, +/− state marker, measure-capped answer) — fully operable with zero script, rows answer :active on touch by construction. The optional enhancer eases the disclosure and stands aside under reduced motion.

The argument spine's proof peak (~40%): the index+card hybrid — a headliner tier of 3/4 media cards over the full bill as divided index rows. The card frame fill survives a paired component's clip wrapper by construction. Layout only; interaction is the paired components' job.

components.whenToUse: Headline/statement entrance: masked line reveal, staggered. The tier's default over a per-char fade.
A film still the visitor drives — scroll or pointer maps to video currentTime. The operable-spectacle signature; never an autoplay loop.

components.winner: Dennis Snellenberg, Wix Mouse Parallax Wonderland
components.whenToUse: Multi-layer depth under the pointer: [data-depth] layers shift a few px at differential rates (lerp 0.1, ~20px max — depth, never drift; negative depth moves opposite). Fine-pointer only; DORMANT on touch — the winner convention, depth comes from scroll there.

components.winner: the cosmic push-in class (Apple-lineage pinned scrub; MERIDIAN v2 validation)
components.whenToUse: The scroll dive: a pinned full-bleed media scales toward a targeted focal point (the moon, the product, the plate) as the track scrolls — reversible, compositor-only; optional fade hand-off at the end of the travel. A spectacle-tier scroll texture.
Smoothed-scroll foundation for scrubbed/pinned reveals. Enhances only when Lenis is present; native scroll otherwise; null instance under reduced-motion.
Fixed nav: transparent over the hero, gains ground on scroll, hides on scroll-down and reveals on scroll-up.
Earned custom cursor that does real work: magnetic snap to [data-ad-magnetic]. Fine-pointer only; native on touch and under reduced-motion. Use sparingly, never as decoration.
CTA/button label two-line wipe swap on hover/focus. Hard-edged, restrained.
Inline text links: accent recolor + underline wipe on hover/focus.
Nav links / short labels: per-character rollover on hover/focus, staggered. Keeps a clean accessible name via aria-label.
Media uncover on scroll-in: animated clip-path (inset or ellipse) with a scale settle. Wrap an /

The tier's text signature, two channels: scrub (words brighten dim-to-bright as the block traverses the viewport — reversible emphasis on always-legible copy) and entrance (words arrive as accent, settle to ink, fire-once). Preserves inline markup (semantic-accent terms compose).
Key terms marked [data-ad-term] carry the accent — colour does the reading; terms ignite on first view. Composes inside text-emphasis-fill blocks.
Masked per-char assemble entrance for short display headings — the richer second reveal beyond kinetic-reveal's line mask. Keeps a clean accessible name via aria-label.

components.winner: Terminal Industries, Bruno Simon, Depo Luxe
components.whenToUse: Stat/counter roll on scroll-into-view — the markup carries the true final value (visible with no JS), tabular-nums, format-preserving (1,344 · 99.7% · +412 yr).
Fixed film-grain + optional vignette overlay for a poster grade. Compositor-clean, pointer-events:none, low opacity. Restraint.
components.init: awardGrainGrade.init(root, { opacity, animate, blend, vignette, zIndex })

components.winner: Truekind, Siena Film Foundation, Terminal Industries, Son Daven, Lando Norris, Sui
components.whenToUse: The universal primary-CTA move: full-token flood + label inversion on hover/focus — fill (direct pole swap) or wipe (a panel rises from the bottom edge). Never a pale tint. Pairs with masked-label-swap when the label should roll too.
The default figure response: contained zoom to 1.1 (felt, never a 1-3% twitch) + a companion cue — tint, scrim lift, or caption rise — on hover and focus-within.

components.winner: Depo Luxe, Son Daven, Terminal Industries, Siena
components.whenToUse: The living index: hovered row lights with an accent rule and surfaced metadata while siblings dim to 45% — the spotlight list for archives, work indexes, ledgers.
Gallery spotlight: the hovered item sharpens while siblings blur and dim. Fine-pointer only; keep galleries under ~10 items (blur repaints).
The treated-image reveal: a clip wipe arrives grayscale, colour floods in late — two beats. Use over clip-reveal when the build's imagery is graded/archival.

The token-driven WebGL texture layer — gradient-mesh, noise-field, or pointer-ripple painted from the DESIGN.md palette. A living ground behind real DOM content, never the hero; CSS-gradient fallback, static frame under reduced-motion.

components.winner: Terminal Industries, Bruno Simon, Depo Luxe
components.whenToUse: The numeric counter loader: rolls with real load progress, recolors to the accent near 100, lifts as a curtain. Authored hidden — no-JS never blocks the page. Pair its handoff with the hero's entrance.
The cover wipe that rhymes with the loader: play(fn) covers the viewport, runs the swap at full cover, wipes away. For section/route swaps; returns a promise; instant cut under reduced-motion.
components.init: awardCurtain.init(root, { zIndex, color }) -> { play(fn, opts), destroy }

components.winner: Terminal Industries (radial glow); premium-patterns perpetual-micro canon
components.whenToUse: The third channel — the page breathes at rest: glow, float, shimmer, or pulse at ambient amplitude, paused off-screen and on hidden tabs. Opt elements in via data-ad-idle.

components.winner: Igloo Inc (frost panels); the Liquid Glass surface canon
components.whenToUse: The spatial-organic signature surface: backdrop-blur glass with the inset highlight and concentric nested radii (Doppelrand); opaque fallback keeps text readable without blur support.
The blurred accent under-glow that lifts a card — breathes up on hover/focus; the blur never animates, only opacity (compositor-clean).
The cursor-tracked border light: an accent glow masked to the card's 1px edge follows the pointer. Fine-pointer only; the static hairline is the complete touch/rest look.
The physical press: hard offset shadow that lifts on hover and collapses on press — 125ms linear, a mechanism not a gesture. The :active press IS the tap answer.
The sticker sheet: children rest at alternating rotations (-2.5/2.5/-1 by parity) and straighten on hover — the brutalist figure identity, legible with no pointer at all.
Short labels/links/data-chrome decode from charset noise to the true string (entrance once; hover replay variant). Never on paragraphs; mono targets keep width stable.
The RGB channel-split display heading — token-clean ghost clones clip-jitter in 600ms BURSTS every 5-9s (never continuous; bursts are punctuation), IO- and visibility-gated.

Section form. Costumed threshold: an ENTER gate (doubles as the sound gate) over a full-viewport splash; lifts to reveal the site. Authored `hidden` so no-JS shows the page; focus-trapped while open, released on enter. Pair the enter control with fill-invert-cta or masked-label-swap — a dead ENTER hover is the first impression lost.
Section form. Hold-and-drag horizontal strip of treated stills, each with a jury pull-quote. Native overflow-x at rest; grab-drag + release momentum as enhancement; never hijacks vertical scroll.
Section form. Cinematic bookend footer: inverts the page palette once at the close, oversized wordmark rises on enter. Legible in both palette states.

components.winner: Oryzo AI by Lusion (camera through true Z-depth around and into one object), Explore Primland (aerial camera over terrain), ERA by Vide Infra (scroll-zoom into architectural detail)
components.whenToUse: The true-3D camera dive: scroll progress scrubs a real camera PATH — position + lookAt (+ optional FOV) keyframes, linearly interpolated, inertially eased so the subject keeps moving between ticks, reversible. Hand it a Three.js-compatible camera, an engine-agnostic onUpdate(state), or both — it never imports Three. Optional fade hand-off dissolves the pinned frame over the last of the travel; static final frame under reduced-motion. Reach for this when the depth is a genuine 3D scene; dolly-zoom is the 2.5D DOM cousin — a pinned media scaled toward a focal point.
components.init: awardScrollCameraDive.init(root, { keyframes, camera, onUpdate, travel, ease, fadeLast }) -> { destroy }

components.winner: Lando Norris ("Load Norris" in-brand loader), Messenger (5.7MB Three.js init gate), Oryzo / Cartier / ERA (heavy WebGL scenes)
components.whenToUse: The immersive archetype's designed first-load state: progress tied to REAL asset loading (opts.assets counted, a Three.js LoadingManager-like { onProgress } adapter, document.fonts.ready — all combinable), a builder-authored brand mark where a spinner would sit, a reveal hand-off to the hero — a raw spinner is the archetype's first-impression defect. Shown progress is the slower of real load and a time-eased floor, so a fast load reads as a designed beat, never a flash. Optionally becomes the ENTER / sound-unlock gate (autoplay policy needs a user gesture; onComplete reports userGesture). Rhymes with curtain-transition — the exit reveal is the same cover-and-hand-off grammar as the curtain's wipe; pair the hand-off with the hero's entrance. Authored hidden — no-JS never blocks the page.
components.init: awardBrandedPreloader.init(root, { selector, assets, track, fonts, min, enter, onComplete }) -> { destroy }

components.winner: Messenger by abeto, Egg Hunt by Merci-Michel, Bruno Simon
components.whenToUse: Per-object hover/tap/hit states for interactive meshes INSIDE a WebGL scene — the axis the DOM-element canon omits. Wire opts.hitTest to your raycaster; the scene paints its own visual per state: an emissive lift or a thin outline on 'hover', scale ≈1.05 with a snap on 'hit', flat on 'rest'. Non-interactive meshes return null and never light. Fine pointer gets hover + a pointer cursor; touch fires the raycast on the tap (no hover); opts.proxies renders keyboard-reachable focusable buttons for every scene action. Under reduced-motion the state machine still runs — swap animated highlights for instant state swaps.
components.init: awardRaycastObjectState.init(root, { hitTest, onState, onActivate, cueMs, proxies })

components.winner: Cartier Watches & Wonders 2025 (Immersive Garden + 60fps), Hubtown (Unseen Studio)
components.whenToUse: The staged-rooms spine: an ordered array of discrete 3D scenes sharing one canvas + one camera rig, scroll transitioning the camera room-to-room 'like a museum after hours' (one alcove per artifact). The rig owns only the scroll -> room-index/progress/transition math and emits it via callbacks + the bubbling `ad:room` event; the delegated scene owns all rendering. Reduced-motion snaps to a discrete slideshow. Distinct from engine-world (one continuous scene) and portrait-procession (DOM over a static-framed canvas).
components.init: awardRoomsProcession.init(root, { onRoom, onProgress, onTransition, window, ease })

components.whenToUse: The gallery-stack's continuation carry: a clip-path inset opens bottom-up WHILE the media scales inversely to scroll progress — welded to scroll position, re-fires every pass both directions. Distinct from clip-reveal (fire-once) and dolly-zoom (pinned focal scale).

components.winner: Cyd Stumpel — Portfolio 2025; Stefan Vitasovic; Pacome Pertant
components.whenToUse: Multi-view portfolio momentum carrier: the home→project-detail swap crossfades/morphs instead of hard-cutting — native View Transitions when available (shared view-transition-name elements morph), WAAPI container crossfade otherwise. Imperative: call go(fn) around the swap; input-agnostic so it carries on touch.

The gallery-stack loader/intro: a stylistic linear 1→100 count (2.8s), an ~.8s slow-in fade, then a scramble-decode type assembly over the main gallery (per-element durations cycling Gabriel's verified list, expo-out locks). Distinct from counter-loader's honest load-gated roll + curtain wipe.
components.init: awardTypeIntroLoader.init(root, { selector, decodeSelector, duration, charset, sessionOnce, onDone })

components.whenToUse: The restraint-compatible cursor slot: a small monochrome ink dot (mode 'dot' — replaces the native cursor, grows over interactive targets, compresses on press) or a lightweight decaying mouse trail behind the native cursor (mode 'trail'). Reads --ad-ink only — no color spectacle; fully dormant on touch and reduced-motion; never gates content or a11y.

The sustained substrate carry: every char of the opted-in blocks joins one document-ordered sequence brightened dim→ink by GLOBAL page progress — the reading text is the continuous thread hero-to-footer. Distinct from text-emphasis-fill (per-word, per-block viewport scrub). Reversible; the 0.45 dim floor keeps copy legible.

components.winner: FlowFest 2025 (boundary-adjacent; beat params illustrative — the pattern is the verified part)
components.whenToUse: The argument spine's in-character loader: a mascot's chat cloud types successive beats at a flat cadence (the ease:none tell) with an optional linear stepped count, holds the hero's resident line until the real load, fades 0.3s, then the nav drops (−102%→0) and the welcome cards stagger. The loader SIGNS its character — never a bare counter.
components.init: awardChatCloudLoader.init(root, { selector, beats, heroLine, charMs, holdMs, nav, stagger, sessionOnce, onDone })

components.whenToUse: The studio-reel loader: the number RATCHETS 0→100 in n discrete jumps (steps(14), ~3s — the jump is the brutalist tell vs counter-loader's smooth roll), gates the last step on the real load, then a clip-path inset() wipe; optionally the full-bleed plate FLIPs into the showreel element so the watched image becomes the hero's media.
components.init: awardSteppedCounterLoader.init(root, { selector, steps, minDuration, flipTo, sessionOnce, onDone })

components.whenToUse: The studio-index loader: progress-becomes-UI. The nav element ITSELF is the loading bar — it rides up to a thin sliver at the viewport top, an accent fill tracks the real load, then the bar grows into the navbar (the nav drops to full height, content fades up). Single-source: the watched element becomes furniture. The nav is authored visible; the page behind stays painted (pre-composed fold).

components.winner: Naked City Films (winner-verified via Codrops; shader numbers illustrative — WebGL-internal on the winner)
components.whenToUse: The restraint-register figure treatment: on hover/focus a raw-WebGL CRT shader dissolves the still into accent-tinted offset R/G/B channels (scanlines, row jitter, noise dissolve), then the buffered video underneath autoplays once the transition completes; leaving reverses and pauses. Tap toggles on touch. No WebGL → the spec's invert(100%) flash ≤0.2s then the video. Distinct from glitch-type (CSS heading split) and figure-hover (contained zoom).
